questions.stem: What energy transformation takes place in a generator?

options.text: Chemical energy to kinetic energy
Kinetic energy to electrical energy
Thermal energy to electrical energy
Electrical energy to kinetic energy

questions.explanation: A generator converts kinetic (rotational) energy into electrical energy using electromagnetic induction. This is the reverse of a motor, which converts electrical energy into kinetic energy.

questions.stem: What type of contact does an AC generator use to connect the rotating coil to the external circuit?

options.text: A transformer
Direct wire connections
Slip rings
A split-ring commutator

questions.explanation: An AC generator uses slip rings, which are two complete metal rings that maintain continuous contact with the brushes. A split-ring commutator is used in DC generators and motors.

questions.stem: At what position of the coil in an AC generator is the induced voltage at its maximum?

options.text: When the coil is vertical (perpendicular to the field)
The voltage is constant at all positions
When the coil is horizontal (parallel to the field)
When the coil is at 45 degrees to the field

questions.explanation: The induced voltage is maximum when the coil is horizontal because the coil sides are cutting through the magnetic field lines at the fastest rate. When vertical, the coil moves parallel to the field and the voltage is zero.

questions.stem: What is the difference between the output of an AC generator and a DC generator?

options.text: A DC generator always produces a perfectly steady voltage
A DC generator does not use magnets
An AC generator produces a voltage that reverses direction, while a DC generator produces a voltage that is always in one direction
An AC generator produces a higher voltage

questions.explanation: An AC generator produces an alternating voltage that reverses direction each half turn. A DC generator uses a split-ring commutator to reverse the connections every half turn, so the output is always in the same direction (pulsating DC).

questions.stem: How can the peak voltage output of a generator be increased?

options.text: By rotating the coil more slowly
By removing the iron core from the coil
By using weaker magnets
By rotating the coil faster, using stronger magnets, or increasing the number of turns

questions.explanation: The induced voltage increases with faster rotation (greater rate of change of flux), stronger magnets (greater flux density), more turns on the coil, or a larger coil area.

questions.stem: What happens to the frequency of the AC output if the generator coil is rotated faster?

options.text: The frequency increases
The frequency is not affected by rotation speed
The frequency stays the same but the voltage increases
The frequency decreases

questions.explanation: Rotating the coil faster increases both the peak voltage and the frequency of the AC output. Each complete rotation produces one full cycle, so more rotations per second means a higher frequency.

questions.stem: Which physical principle does a generator rely on to produce electricity?

options.text: The motor effect
Electromagnetic induction
Static electricity
The heating effect of a current

questions.explanation: A generator works by electromagnetic induction. As the coil rotates in the magnetic field, the changing magnetic flux through the coil induces a voltage across it.
